title: Bathing with Nature – A Forest Walk Experience
summary: A half-day forest bathing walk at Bukit Timah Nature Reserve where youths put their phones away and embrace nature through a nature walk, sensory booklet tasks, team station games and outdoor tea appreciation. Participants get attuned to their senses and surroundings, learn to regulate emotions and embrace the discomfort of being out in nature, and experience new sights, sounds and smells in a world not normally viewed.
objectives: Embrace nature and view it in a different light as participants get attuned to their surroundings
Experience new sights, sounds and smells while immersed in a world not normally viewed
Use exposure to the outdoors for emotional regulation, learning to attune to the senses
Embrace the uncomfortability of being out in nature
Switch off from the outside world (phones away) and live in the moment, becoming more aware of surroundings and of themselves

sessions.title: Meet and phone check-in
sessions.activities:
9:00-9:15AM Meet at designated point (Bukit Timah Nature Reserve main entrance)
Participants are encouraged to store their phones away, either in their bags or in a keep-safe bag, for the rest of the activity
sessions.materials: Keep-safe bag for phones, water bottles

sessions.title: Introduction and icebreaker: My Favourite … (nature scavenger hunt)
sessions.activities:
9:15-9:45AM Introduction to activity and icebreaker
Facilitator names a prompt (item/descriptor/genre) for participants to find, e.g. roundest, smoothest, shiniest; your favourite rock/leaf/fruit; something green/rough/crunchy
Participants get a fixed amount of time to search their surroundings for an item matching the description (not limited in what they can use)
Participants share about the item they picked and the thought process behind their selection
No prizes for the best item: participants pick based on what they like, not what they think will win, and explore freely

sessions.title: Forest Buddy booklet explanation + water/bio break
sessions.activities:
9:45-10:00AM Introduce the Forest Buddy Pack (mindfulness nature kit: booklet, stickers, markers, small pack of tea leaves) and explain the booklet and its purpose
Booklet tasks to complete on the walk: search for a unique leaf/flower and take a photo of it; take a photo of 5 different animals/insects; find the tallest tree; record a bird call; a scenery that speaks to you
Completing the booklet earns a reward (notebook)
Water/bio break
sessions.materials: Forest Buddy Pack (booklet, stickers, markers, tea leaves) x1 per pax, writing materials, notebooks (completion reward)

sessions.title: Walk to first station
sessions.activities:
10:00-10:30AM Commence walk to first station
Participants work on their Forest Buddy booklet tasks while on the trail

sessions.title: First station activity (group activity at summit)
sessions.activities: 10:30-11:00AM Station game at the summit, chosen from the five station games (Photo Challenge, Tarp Flip, Lava Crossing, Bull Ring, Helium Straw); 3 of the 5 are used depending on group size and weather on the day
sessions.materials: Materials for the chosen station game (see notes)

sessions.title: Walk to second station
sessions.activities:
11:00-11:30AM Commence walk to second station
Continue booklet tasks along the trail

sessions.title: Second station activity
sessions.activities: 11:30AM-12:00PM Station game chosen from the five station games (see notes)
sessions.materials: Materials for the chosen station game (see notes)

sessions.title: Walk to lunch
sessions.activities: 12:00-12:30PM Commence walk to lunch

sessions.title: Debrief and lunch
sessions.activities: 12:30-1:30PM Debrief and lunch at last station (lunch at Springleaf)

materials: Mindfulness Nature Kit / Forest Buddy Pack x30 (printed booklet, stickers, markers, small pack of tea leaves)
Pose reference sheets and camera/smartphone (Photo Challenge)
One large tarp per team (Tarp Flip)
Obstacle course layout and crossing materials e.g. planks, ropes or foam tiles (Lava Crossing)
Strings, central ring/platform, assorted balls (Bull Ring)
One lightweight drinking straw per team (Helium Straw)
budget: S$289.50 stated total for 30 pax (S$9.65 per pax); itemised: paper cups S$3 (1 set of 50), Pocari Sweat packets S$31.50 (3 x S$10.50), Outdoor Care Kit S$15 (30 x S$0.50), Mindfulness Nature Kit S$60 (30 x S$2), lunch at TenderFresh S$240 (30 x S$8) - note the itemised lines add up to S$349.50
riskNotes:
Area: floor may be wet and slippery, especially after heavy rain; no running or playing on the hike; loose rocks and soil - avoid climbing or going off trail; steep climbs at points - hold onto rope/rail, no playing at such locations; covered shoes at all times (no slippers, flip-flops, Crocs, open-toed sandals).
Wildlife: many wild monkeys - keep safe distance when taking photos; no loose plastic bags, food or water bottles, everything in a backpack or sling bag; do not feed, scare or approach any animals; respect nature, do not pluck, remove or damage any wildlife, leave the place better than you found it.
Other: drink lots of water; use insect spray/medicated oil if needed; be mindful of surroundings when taking photos; do not climb, crawl under or hang over any edge, cliff or structure.
Mitigation: recce the site beforehand, identify and flag hazard areas, brief participants and demarcate off-limit areas; explain and demonstrate all equipment before issuing; ensure activities suit participants' age; check weather forecast, wet weather plans for each activity; avoid dangerous tools if not age appropriate, adult supervision for younger participants or those with certain needs, use less dangerous alternatives.
Wet weather plan: multiple shelter and rest points along the route and a poncho for each participant; light rain - continue once wet weather gear is on; heavy rain - switch to sheltered activity until rain stops, activity may be cut short with main focus on tea appreciation; if rain persists, do tea appreciation in the shelter and give hot water to warm up. Wet weather activities: group finger bridge game (balance sticks between two fingers, restart if a stick falls, goal of 20 sticks) and reflective photography (photos using reflections in water, from nature to selfies).
Psychological safety: sharing is optional; no fixing or judging rule; clear group agreements; facilitator models vulnerability appropriately.
Emergency contacts: Jeremy 92243993; Lyndon (number not given).
outcomes:
Intended outcomes: participants gain greater appreciation for nature, increased awareness of their surroundings and experience nature in a new way; they get a chance to escape their normal environment and explore nature.
Success criteria: participants complete their booklet and actively participate in all activities.
Feedback: positive feedback from survey and verbal confirmation.
Observable indicator: greater awareness of their environment.
notes:
Date and venue: 15 Aug, 9AM-1:30PM, Bukit Timah Nature Reserve (outdoors setting). Meeting point: entrance to Bukit Timah Nature Reserve. Transport: nil. F&B: lunch and refreshments.

Facilitators: main facilitators Jeremy and Lyndon; mindfulness trainers May and Ya Wen.

Attire: light comfortable clothes, shorts, covered shoes, hat (optional).

Core youth need: youths are growing up increasingly sealed away from the outdoors, linked to lowered immunity, depression, irritability and lower stress tolerance, while stress levels are at an all-time high and safe outlets for expression are shrinking. The forest asks only for presence: it lowers anxiety, builds stress tolerance through small low-stakes stressors, offers a judgement-free space to speak, cry, laugh or stay silent, and rebuilds focus by removing digital distractions. "In a world that constantly asks young people to do more, this activity invites them to be still."

Core competencies: primary focus is exposure to the outdoors for emotional regulation, attuning to the senses and embracing the uncomfortability of being in nature. Activities named for building this: nature walk, outdoor tea appreciation and sensory mapping.

Icebreaker: My Favourite … (nature-based scavenger hunt), purpose: introduce the idea of interacting with nature. Suits the age group because youths need hands-on experiences with few restrictions while being guided enough for a sense of safety and direction.

Mindfulness element: framed as increasing awareness of environment, senses and surroundings through observational activities (phones away, booklet sensory tasks, tea appreciation).

Station games (3 of 5 used depending on group size and weather):
Photo Challenge - teams replicate a set of group pose reference photos as accurately and creatively as possible within the time; points for number, precision and originality (communication, coordination, attention to detail).
Tarp Flip - team stands on a fully unfolded tarp and folds it into the smallest possible area without anyone stepping off (problem-solving, balance, spatial awareness, teamwork).
Lava Crossing - cross an obstacle course using planks, ropes or foam tiles without touching the ground; touching means penalty or restart from checkpoint (strategic planning, resource management, trust, physical coordination).
Bull Ring - move balls of different sizes to a target using a central ring controlled by strings held by each participant, without dropping any (precision, synchronisation, patience, collective focus).
Helium Straw - lower a straw from chest height to the ground with every member keeping index-finger contact; restart if anyone loses contact (patience, non-verbal communication, coordination, trust).

Plan inconsistencies to check: the overview says 4 stations but the timeline has 2 station slots, while the games section says 3 of 5 games are used; tea appreciation and sensory mapping are mentioned but not scheduled in the timeline; lunch is budgeted at TenderFresh but the timeline says Springleaf; 9AM-1:30PM is 270 minutes vs the 240 minutes stated; ponchos and notebooks are not in the budget.

Target ages ticked: 10-12 (Upper Primary), 13-16 (Secondary), 17-19 (Upper Sec/ITE/JC).

Format ticked: One-Off Session.

Competencies ticked: Regulate Emotions Before Acting; Embrace Discomfort Without Escape; Define Self-Worth Beyond Performance.

Icebreaker ticks: purpose Reduce Awkwardness, Encourage Interaction, Normalise Sharing; time 15 minutes.

Mindfulness ticks: objective Awareness And Focus, Reflection And Insight, Attention Control; type Sensory Grounding, Mindful Listening Or Speaking; infused at Multiple Points; total time 11-15 minutes.

Observable indicators ticked: Increased Participation.

Source: Bathing_with_nature.docx

title: The Vocal Palette (Songcraft Studio)
summary: A singing and voice programme teaching basic breathing and vocal techniques to increase awareness of one's own breathing and voice. Designed for upper primary and secondary youths, it builds greater self-awareness and control over voice and body, a positive self-identity, and confidence in themselves.
objectives: Learn basic breathing and vocal techniques
Increase awareness of one's own breathing and voice
Develop greater self-awareness and control over voice and body
Increase breathing and vocal control
Build better confidence in themselves and a positive self-identity

sessions.title: Arrival
sessions.activities: 17:00-17:05 Participants arrive

sessions.title: Introduction and icebreaker: Don't Forget the Lyrics
sessions.activities:
17:05-17:20 Introduction and icebreaker
Icebreaker is not done in groups
Participants are arranged in an open mic setting where anyone is able to challenge the song
Participants take turns listening to a portion of a song
Lyrics are provided up to the cut-out portion
Once the music stops, participants have 1 minute to recall the lyrics

sessions.title: Breathing exercise
sessions.activities:
17:20-17:45 Breathing exercise
Unlike mindful breathing, vocal breath exercise focuses on the diaphragm and emphasises a full breath
Participants either lie down or rest against a wall
Take deep slow breaths while holding onto their hips; feel the sides and back expand with each breath
Continue in counts of 4, focusing on the breathing in and out motion

sessions.title: Vocal warm-ups
sessions.activities:
17:45-18:10 Vocal warm-ups
Lip trills (bubbles): relax lips and blow air through them to create a motor-like sound; move up and down your comfortable range; releases tension and connects breathing to sound
Humming: start with "Mmm" on a comfortable pitch; feel the vibration in your face/mask area; glide gently up and down your range
Sirens: start at your lowest comfortable note and slide smoothly to your highest on "oo" or "ee"; never push at the extremes
Five-note scales (major): start on a comfortable note (try C, D or E); sing Do-Re-Mi-Fa-Sol-Fa-Mi-Re-Do; use different vowels "Ma-me-mi-mo-mu"

sessions.title: Vocal practice
sessions.activities:
18:10-18:45 Vocal practices
Articulation practice: tongue twisters at a comfortable pitch; "Red leather, yellow leather" slowly then faster; "Unique New York" focusing on clear consonants
Simple songs: choose songs within a limited range (5-6 notes), such as folk songs, children's songs or simple pop choruses; focus on maintaining consistent tone rather than volume

sessions.title: Debrief and reflection
sessions.activities: 18:45-18:55 Debrief and reflection

sessions.title: Pack up
sessions.activities:
18:55-19:00 Pack up
19:00 End of session

budget: ~S$10 per session (light refreshments); S$1 per pax; 2 sessions = S$20 per run
riskNotes:
Centre risks: fall risk in centre (climbing, running and slip risks). Mitigation: give proper rules and instructions for all activities; set ground rules and consequences for breaking rules.
During activity: participants might get injured (cuts, bruises, other injuries). Mitigation: ensure proper supervision where risk is present; give instructions for proper handling; never leave high-risk objects unattended.
Voice care: ensure participants drink lots of fluids to prevent throat injuries; never push at the extremes of range.
Psychological safety: sharing is optional; no fixing or judging rule stated; clear group agreements; facilitator models vulnerability appropriately.
Emergency contact: Jeremy, 92243993 (second contact not filled in).
outcomes:
Intended outcomes: improved proficiency in vocal skills; increased self-confidence and self-identity.
Success criteria: visible improvement in breath control and self-confidence.
Feedback: survey and verbal feedback.
Observable indicators: increased participation.
notes:
Venue: Brahm Centre @ Aljunied (youth centre setting), starting 17:00. Date TBC. Transport: nil. Food: light refreshments.

Facilitators: Jeremy (main facilitator).

Attire: comfortable loose clothes.

Target age (as ticked): 10-12 Upper Primary and 13-16 Secondary. Format ticked: Structured Programme (5-8 sessions), although the budget is costed for 2 sessions.

Core youth need: youth need to develop a positive self-identity separate from the stigma of "rental flat" or "low-income" and be seen for their potential, not their postal code; access to affordable, youth-friendly, destigmatised mental health support. The activity targets self-identity, mental and emotional wellbeing and social interaction skills.

Why it matters: young people are at an impressionable age where negative or antisocial influences can have lasting effects; replacing these with positive, prosocial activities guides them toward a healthier mindset.

Core competencies: none ticked. Primary competency focus: greater self-awareness and control over voice and body, built through breathing exercises, vocal techniques and focus on vocal placement.

Icebreaker: Don't Forget the Lyrics, 15 minutes; purpose: reduce awkwardness, encourage interaction, energise the group. Relatable because youths are attuned to current music and TikTok trends, while adding an "old school" element to reflect and discover.

Mindfulness element: objectives awareness and focus, attention control; types breath awareness, body awareness/movement, mindful listening or speaking; infused at multiple points; 11-15 minutes total.

Source: Proposal 3 for youth connect (The Vocal Palette).docx

title: Build with AI
summary: A four-Saturday hands-on series that gives students more confidence to build with AI and guidance on creating apps, brand kits and marketing content with it. Each youth works on a self-chosen, personally meaningful project, moving from passive AI use to creation. Participants leave with a portfolio of 1-4 finished projects and a more intentional, critical relationship with AI tools.
objectives: Allow students more confidence to build with AI
Give them guidance on how to proceed more easily to create brand kits, marketing strategies and apps with AI
Think independently of trends: practise directing AI rather than blindly following it, developing judgement about when to trust, edit or reject AI output
Define self-worth beyond performance: build self-worth through creating something tangible rather than through grades or social validation

sessions.title: Icebreaker: Wacko + Real or Not
sessions.activities:
Wacko:
Sit everyone in a circle. Choose one person to be "it" in the centre with a rolled-up newspaper; their objective is to hit the person whose name has been called before that person can call another name (all hits on the legs only).
Name rules: you cannot call the same person who called you; you cannot call the person in the centre; the person you call must be present in the circle.
Begin with introductions: each person gives their name and one interesting fact (e.g. "What is your favourite ice-cream?" or a question related to the lesson).
Explain the rules, then call out a name (e.g. "Ken"). Ken must call another name BEFORE the person in the middle whacks him.
Whoever is whacked, breaks a rule or makes a mistake moves to the centre; the person who just came out begins the next round by calling a name.
Anyone who ends up in the centre three times performs a forfeit (sing a song, dance, tell a joke).
Real or Not:
Participants log on to Kahoot and enter the game pin shown on screen.
Answer questions as a team; the highest cumulative score wins a prize.
sessions.materials: Rolled-up newspaper, Kahoot game, screen, prize

sessions.title: Session 1 - Basics of AI App Development
sessions.activities:
1. What even is an app? (20 min) - Demystify how AI turns a sentence into working software, with one live "prompt-to-app" demo to hook the room.
2. Idea sprint (25 min) - Each participant picks a real problem in their life and shapes it into a one-line app brief with AI.
3. First build (45 min) - Prompt an app into existence from a starter template and watch it appear live on screen.
4. Iterate & personalise (40 min) - Change colours, copy and features by talking to the AI; learn to give feedback that lands.
5. Ship & show (30 min) - Publish to a shareable link and demo to the group. Everyone leaves with a URL.
sessions.materials: Laptops (own), starter template, speaker and microphone, extension cables

sessions.title: Session 2 - Intermediate AI App Development
sessions.activities:
1. From toy to tool (20 min) - Recap the basics, then read what the AI actually generated so it stops feeling like magic.
2. Design the data (30 min) - Plan what the app needs to remember, then have AI scaffold a database around it.
3. Wire it up (50 min) - Connect storage and pull in a live external API (weather, transit, or a public dataset).
4. Debug like a pro (40 min) - Things break, good. Learn to read errors and pair with AI to fix them quickly.
5. Deploy & demo (40 min) - Ship to the real internet, then present the build and one hard problem solved.
sessions.materials: Laptops (own), speaker and microphone, extension cables

sessions.title: Session 3 - AI in App Design
sessions.activities:
1. Design thinking, fast (25 min) - Pick a cause, define an audience, and frame the design problem. Good design starts before the visuals.
2. Moodboard with AI (30 min) - Generate directions, palettes and references, then curate. Taste is the skill being trained.
3. Brand & visuals (45 min) - Create a logo, key imagery and a poster, learning to art-direct the prompts.
4. Idea to interface (40 min) - Turn the brand into a real landing-page mockup and preview it as a live page.
5. Gallery critique (20 min) - Walk the wall, give and take feedback, the part that builds a designer's eye.
sessions.materials: Laptops (own), speaker and microphone, extension cables

sessions.title: Session 4 - AI in Content Creation
sessions.activities:
1. Message before medium (25 min) - Decide who you're talking to and what you want them to feel. Strategy first, tools second.
2. Script & copy (35 min) - Draft a hook, script and captions with AI, then rewrite in your own voice so it isn't generic.
3. Make the assets (45 min) - Generate visuals, a voiceover and short video clips from the script.
4. Edit & assemble (35 min) - Cut it into a polished 30-60 second piece with captions and music.
5. Showcase reel (20 min) - Play the finished pieces back to back. Everyone leaves with content they can post today.
sessions.materials: Laptops (own), speaker and microphone, extension cables

sessions.title: Feedback (end of each session)
sessions.activities: Participants complete the feedback form in the last 15 minutes of each session.

materials: Extension cables (one per table for charging)
budget: Not specified (itemised budget blank, total estimated cost "-"); F&B is light refreshments, students bring their own laptops
riskNotes:
Centre risk: fall risk in centre (climbing, running and slip risks). Mitigation: give proper rules and instructions for all activities; set ground rules and consequences for breaking them.

During activity: participants might get cuts, bruises or other injuries (e.g. during Wacko; all hits on the legs only). Mitigation: proper supervision for each activity where risk is present; instructions for proper handling; never leave high-risk objects unattended.

Overreliance on AI after the programme: some students may become over-reliant on AI, leading to laziness or unwillingness to think for themselves. Mitigation: tell students the dos and don'ts with AI, plus security precautions (e.g. not inputting API keys into AI).

Psychological safety: sharing is optional; non-judgemental if prompts or final output don't turn out as expected; clear group agreements.

Emergency contacts: not filled in.
outcomes:
Intended outcomes: confidence to build with AI independently; a portfolio of 1-4 finished projects (app, brand kit, content piece); a more intentional, critical relationship with AI tools.

Success criteria: 80% of participants create a deliverable each session; at least 50% of participants are willing to share their idea at the end of the session.

Feedback: feedback form completed in the last 15 minutes of each session.
notes:
Target ages ticked on the form: 13–16 (Secondary) and 17–19 (Upper Sec / ITE / JC). Format ticked: Short series (2–4 sessions).

Venue: Brahm Centre @ Aljunied (meeting location Brahm @ Aljunied; no transport; light refreshments).

Facilitators: Liang Tze (main facilitator); Jeremy (staff on site).

Attire: comfortable clothes; jacket in case it is cold.

Youth need addressed: most youths use AI passively (chatting, scrolling, homework shortcuts) without learning to build or create with it, leaving them under-equipped for a future where AI fluency is a baseline skill; without guidance their AI use skews toward consumption rather than creation, which can affect focus, originality, confidence and even grades.

Why it matters for this age group: youths are forming their sense of capability and direction for study and work; hands-on creative mastery builds real confidence and agency rather than anxiety or dependence. Some have heard about AI but, due to high cost, are unsure or afraid to use it to create.

Core competencies: Think Independently Of Trends + Define Self-Worth Beyond Performance. By producing real, personal projects (not just prompting for answers), youths practise directing AI rather than blindly following it like their friends, and build self-worth through creating something tangible.

How youths are involved: each youth works on a self-chosen, personally meaningful project across the sessions: hands-on building, prompting, giving/receiving peer feedback, and presenting.

Icebreaker suitability: Wacko suits the 13-19 age group as fast-paced, high-energy physical play that circumvents teenage self-consciousness; Real or Not on Kahoot leverages digital literacy, sparks healthy competition and meets the need for social validation without causing anxiety.

Mindfulness element: participants reflect on how their app will benefit end users or the problem, and stay mindful of what they do throughout the session.

Session content: the four session run-sheets were embedded as images in the original document and were transcribed from them.

Source: AI_Programme_Liang_Tze.docx

title: Superstar: ME - A 3-Day Self-Worth Discovery Programme
summary: A 6-session indoor programme over 3 days at Brahm Centre Aljunied that uses games, hands-on activities and guided reflection to help youths discover and celebrate six dimensions of self: Physical, Intellectual, Emotional, Social, Personal and Temporal. Participants build self-worth, emotional regulation, independent thinking, social connection and resilience, and leave with concrete tools such as a Pause Button, calm jar, conversation cards and a worth statement.
duration: 3 days, 2 sessions per day (120-150 min per session)
objectives: Discover and celebrate six dimensions of self: Physical, Intellectual, Emotional, Social, Personal and Temporal
Sleep Well For Better Focus: understand sleep hygiene and commit to a pre-bed routine (Session 1, Physical)
Think Independently Of Trends: question popular beliefs and weigh opposing views (Session 2, Intellectual)
Regulate Emotions Before Acting: notice, breathe and choose a response (Session 3, Emotional)
Start And Conduct Conversations: open, sustain and close conversations with confidence (Session 4, Social)
Define Self-Worth Beyond Performance: separate who they are from what they achieve (Session 5, Personal)
Embrace Discomfort Without Escape: build resilience by reflecting on past, present and future discomforts (Session 6, Temporal)

sessions.title: Day 1 opening: registration, introduction and icebreaker
sessions.activities:
9:00-9:15AM Meet at Brahm Centre Aljunied for registration and check-in
9:15-9:45AM Introduction to programme: overview, group agreements and icebreaker Two Truths and a Dream - each participant thinks of two TRUE statements about themselves and one DREAM or aspiration; going around the circle, each shares all three without revealing which is which; the group guesses which is the dream; the participant reveals and briefly explains one truth or their dream. Facilitator note: no wrong answers, the dream can be big or small, serious or silly; the goal is to practise sharing and listening in a supportive environment
9:45-10:00AM Superstar:ME Journal introduction and explanation of the booklet, water and bio break, phones stored in bags or the keep-safe box

sessions.activities:

Main Event: My Sleep Sanctuary - 3D Diorama - build a small diorama of their ideal sleep environment (bed, calming colours, personal touches); on the back write a Sleep Pledge of three things they will do 30 minutes before bed
10:45-11:00AM Water and bio break
11:00-11:30AM Cool Down: Sleep Detective Log - receive a weekly sleep log template; group discusses barriers to good sleep and brainstorms practical solutions
Spotlight: set a bedtime alarm 30 minutes before sleep. Mantra: "Rest is not weakness. Rest is my superpower for focus."
Journal reflection prompt
sessions.materials: Portable speaker, small cardboard boxes, coloured paper, markers, glue, scissors, printed sleep log template

9:00-9:15AM Registration and check-in

9:45-10:00AM Journal, water and bio break, phone storage

sessions.title: Session 5: Personal Self - Define Self-Worth Beyond Performance
sessions.activities:
10:00-10:45AM Warm-Up: The Achievement vs. Identity Sort - draw slips with statements and place them into two labelled bins, Achievements and Identity, to highlight the difference between what they do and who they are
Main Event: The Unshakeable Core - Clay Sculpture - sculpt a core object representing their intrinsic self, something that stays true even if all achievements and recognition were stripped away; paint it a single colour to symbolise its unchanging nature
10:45-11:00AM Water and bio break
11:00-11:30AM Cool Down: The Worth Statement - write one sentence declaring their worth independent of performance on a decorative card, placed with the sculpture
Spotlight: place sculpture and Worth Statement somewhere visible and repeat the statement when measuring worth by outcome. Mantra: "My worth is inherent. I am not my performance."
sessions.materials: Statement slips, two labelled bins, air-dry clay, paint, decorative cards

sessions.title: Day 3 lunch and afternoon re-group
sessions.activities:
11:30AM-12:30PM Lunch break with packed lunch and supervised free time or journaling
12:30-12:45PM Afternoon re-group and short grounding exercise

sessions.title: Session 6: Temporal Self - Embrace Discomfort Without Escape
sessions.activities:
12:45-1:00PM Introduction to the afternoon theme
1:00-1:45PM Warm-Up: The Discomfort Timeline - Human Graph - stand on a rope timeline where they feel they are in handling discomfort; share one thing learned from a past uncomfortable experience
Main Event: The Discomfort Map - Indoor Obstacle Course - complete a low-key indoor obstacle course whose stations represent different types of discomfort; then draw a visual map with symbols for past discomforts survived and future discomforts anticipated, writing beside future symbols "I survived before. I can face this too."
1:45-2:00PM Water and bio break
2:00-2:30PM Cool Down: The Courage Capsule - write on separate slips one past discomfort that made them stronger, one current discomfort and one future discomfort to face with courage; seal and decorate a small container

3:00-3:15PM Mindfulness closing with guided grounding exercise; closing circle "What is one word that describes how you feel right now?"
3:15-3:30PM Wrap-up and dismissal

materials: Superstar:ME Journal Booklet (1 per pax, A5, 20 pages, B&W printing, stapled)
Art supplies (markers, coloured pencils, glue, scissors)
Tables and chairs arranged for group work
riskNotes:
Psychological safety: sharing is optional; no fixing or judging rule stated; clear group agreements; facilitator models vulnerability appropriately.
Facilitation best practices: use open-ended questions ("What did you notice?" rather than "Did you like it?"); validate all responses without judgment; keep a calm, grounded demeanour; allow silence; adjust pacing to group energy and needs; celebrate small wins and efforts, not just outcomes; model patience, kindness and self-compassion; use participant names.
General mitigation listed: explain and demonstrate all equipment before issuing; ensure activities suit participants' age; avoid dangerous tools if not age appropriate and supervise younger participants or those with certain needs when handling equipment.

outcomes:
Intended outcomes: stronger sense of self-worth across the six dimensions; practical skills in emotional regulation, independent thinking, conversation, resilience and self-compassion; a safe, supportive space to express themselves and connect with peers; concrete tools (Pause Button, calm jar, conversation cards, worth statement) for daily life; a completed personal reflection journal.
Success criteria: participants complete the Superstar:ME Journal (all 6 reflection prompts); actively participate in all 6 sessions; show engagement in discussions and reflections; can articulate at least one personal takeaway; create at least 3 tangible tools.
Feedback collection: pre- and post-programme self-assessment surveys (5-point scale on confidence, emotional regulation, self-worth); facilitator observation notes; verbal sharing during debriefs; written journal reflections; anonymous post-programme feedback form; end-of-programme group reflection circle.
Indicators: applying coping strategies (Pause Button, breathing techniques); intrinsic self-worth not tied to external performance; improved confidence in social interactions; greater comfort with self-reflection.
notes:
Venue: Brahm Centre Aljunied (indoor). Date: not given. Transport: nil. F&B: lunch and refreshments (packed lunch).

Facilitators: Jeremy, Lyndon, Mei Jing, Venessa, Xenon, Erwin, Raymond (depends on session).

Attire: comfortable indoor clothes, covered shoes.

Session structure: each session follows four segments - The Warm-Up (game), The Main Event (hands-on activity), The Cool Down (debrief) and The Spotlight (takeaway action and mantra) - plus a reflection prompt in the Superstar:ME Journal. Phones are stored in bags or a keep-safe box for each session. Journal Pack: journal booklet, coloured markers and pens, stickers, plus session-specific materials.

Core youth need: youths face record stress, anxiety and pressure from academics, social media comparison, peer pressure and an uncertain future; many tie their worth to grades, likes and external validation and lack safe spaces to explore identity and process emotions. "In a world that constantly asks young people to perform, this programme invites them to simply be - and discover that they are enough, exactly as they are."

Core competencies: all six form competencies, one per session; primary emphasis on Define Self-Worth Beyond Performance (clay sculpture, worth statement, reflection) and Regulate Emotions Before Acting (Pause Button, calm jar, role-play).

Icebreaker: Two Truths and a Dream - introduces self-discovery and personal sharing in a low-stakes way; normalises sharing both realities and aspirations without deep emotional disclosure, since youths often feel pressure to present a "perfect" version of themselves.

Mindfulness element: framed as "paying attention to the present moment with kindness and curiosity". Opening grounding (three deep breaths); sensory check-in (5 see, 4 touch, 3 hear, 2 smell, 1 taste); body scan (feet, hands, shoulders, relax); reflective pause after each session ("What is one thing you noticed about yourself today?"); private journaling; closing circle ("one word that describes how you feel right now").

title: Social Entrepreneurship Workshop
summary: A two-day hands-on social entrepreneurship workshop for youths aged 15-18 from youth homes and shelters, built on the IDEA framework (Identify, Design, Execute, Adapt). Groups find the root cause of a given problem, design and craft a minimum viable product with Brahm Centre's art trainers and BOfA mentors, then pitch it to an audience. Participants experience the whole cycle of entrepreneurship and build soft skills like resilience and agile thinking, using AI to complement their learning.
objectives: Identify and analyse real-world social problems using root cause analysis techniques
Generate and evaluate innovative solution ideas using structured ideation tools
Design and curate a product (a minimum viable product) for their chosen social enterprise concept
Communicate effectively by pitching their solution with AI-assisted slide decks and handling Q&A
Collaborate with BOA coaches to move from problem identification to a presentable product within a tight timeline
Learn to pitch to different target groups to sell their ideas, moving beyond presentation slides
Adapt to changes, not giving up and relooking when issues arise

Mentors and facilitators help groups plan a solution they would like to curate; groups able to self-ideate are free to design on their own

outcomes: Groups produce a minimum viable product (or rough prototype shell) by the end of the programme and pitch it in round-robin presentations. Prizes track milestones: Tier 1 at least 1 interest from the public, Tier 2 at least 5, Tier 3 at least 8; special prizes for Most Innovative Product and People's Pick.
notes:
Target participants: youths aged 15-18 from youth homes and shelters. Date: July/August (exact dates not given). Venue: not given.

Framework: IDEA - Identify (and analyse root cause of problems and evaluate ideas), Design (an MVP to showcase their ideas to the audience), Execute (ideas; presenting them and creating a plan), Adapt (to changes, not giving up and relooking when issues arise). Product creation draws on the 5 phases of a design sprint: Understand, Sketch, Decide, Prototype, Validate.

Facilitators and partners: Brahm Centre art trainers; BOfA (BOA) mentors/coaches; school teachers and friends attend the presentations.

Art classes:
Art class 1, Wood craft - good for large, purely physical products; not useful for small, specific details. Suggested problem statement: "How can we make recycled wood into something practical for youths?"

(decorating tables and chairs with decoupage); "How can we create DIY personalised gift boxes which are cheap and unique?"
Art class 3, Sketching - used to teach storyboarding and how to present ideas; not useful for creating or demonstrating products other than for the pitch.
Suggested flow: Session 1 Sketch + Plan Idea, then Session 2 Wood craft OR Decoupage workshop.

Unique aspects: interactive sessions instead of lectures; the whole cycle of entrepreneurship is covered; soft skills like resilience and agile thinking which are highly sought after; AI used to complement learning, giving access to the latest skills.

Plan inconsistencies to check: Day 2 lists "Wrap up on prototyping" 10-11AM and "Launch of Marketplace" 10AM-12PM (overlapping); the slide deck describes a 2-hour product creation session while the Day 1 schedule gives 3 hours (1:30-4:30PM); all prize rewards are TBC; no budget, group size, venue or risk plan given.

title: Mind Craft - Stress Management Programme
summary: An interactive exam-stress workshop for teens that normalises exam anxiety, explains why the brain goes blank under pressure, and teaches silent coping skills for the exam hall plus evidence-based study habits. Participants leave with a personalised, portable toolkit: an Exam Day Blueprint card and a lanyard cue card with their go-to breath, anchor and mantra.
objectives: Normalise exam anxiety and get honest data on participants' biggest fears
Teach the biology of memory retrieval under pressure, and differentiate between pre-exam stress and during-exam stress
Teach coping skills specifically designed for use during an exam, when you cannot leave your seat or make noise
Ditch the all-nighters and teach evidence-based revision techniques that actually reduce stress
Turn knowledge into a personalised, portable toolkit

sessions.title: Welcome & Ice-Breaker: "The Exam Fear Factor"
sessions.activities:
Place 4 large buckets/bowls at the front labelled "Going Blank / Memory Freeze", "Running Out of Time", "Letting My Parents/Teachers Down", "Other".
Give each teen 3 ping-pong balls or crumpled paper balls; they throw them into the bucket that represents their biggest exam fear.
Facilitator script: "Look at that. Every single bucket has balls in it. You are NOT weird, broken, or alone. The fear of going blank is actually your brain's threat-detector misfiring. Today, we are going to hack that system."
sessions.materials: 4 buckets/bowls with labels, ping-pong balls or crumpled paper (3 per teen)

sessions.title: Segment 1: Understanding Exam Stress - "Why does my brain go blank?"
sessions.activities:
1. The "Whiteboard vs. Sticky Notes" Brain Demo (15 min) - A volunteer gets 5 seconds to remember and write a 10-digit number you shout out (e.g. 7482910563). Debrief: Working Memory (the whiteboard) holds only 3-5 things; stress pumps adrenaline which shrinks the whiteboard. The "Sticky Note" fix: Long-Term Memory (the filing cabinet) is infinite; the trick is retrieval practice, actively pulling information out rather than re-reading.
2. The "Stress Timeline" Floor Map (20 min) - Masking-tape timeline on the floor: 1 Month Before, 1 Week Before, Night Before, Morning of Exam, In the Exam Hall, During the Last 10 Minutes. Teens walk the timeline and place symptom cards (e.g. "Can't sleep", "Heart racing", "Stomach cramps", "Mind goes blank", "Sweaty palms", "Overwhelming urge to check phone") where they feel them most. Debrief: chronic stress (weeks before) depletes energy, acute stress (in the hall) triggers fight/flight; they are treated differently.
3. The "A+ vs. Pass" Myth-Busting (15 min) - Two columns on the board: "What I think I need to do" vs. "What actually works". Teens shout out myths (e.g. "I need to study for 6 hours straight"); debunk with science: after 45 minutes of focus the brain stops retaining info; retrieval practice is 50% more effective than re-reading; nervousness is just energy, reframe it as excitement.
sessions.materials: Whiteboard and marker, masking tape, symptom cards

sessions.title: Active Brain Break: "The Revision Shake"
sessions.activities: Play a fast-paced song. Shout out a subject topic (e.g. "Pythagoras!", "Photosynthesis!"); teens do 5 star-jumps while shouting back ONE fact about it. Physically anchors knowledge to movement.

sessions.title: Segment 2: Coping Mechanisms - "The Exam-Hall Rescue Kit"
sessions.activities:
1. The "Silent SOS" Stations (30 min) - 4 stations, teens rotate every 7 minutes; each technique can be done silently at a desk during an exam.
Station A: The "Box Breath" Reset - 4-4-4-4 breathing (inhale 4, hold 4, exhale 4, hold 4) for 2 minutes with a metronome/timer while holding a pencil; do it as soon as the invigilator says "You may begin".
Station B: The "Page Pause" Grounding - palms flat on the desk, feel the surface, press gently, say in your head "This desk is solid. I am solid.", then trace the margin line of the exam paper with a finger.
Station C: The "Brain-Dump" Technique - on spare paper, spend 60 seconds writing everything remembered about a topic before reading the question; practise with a random topic (e.g. "World War 2 causes").
Station D: The "Micro-Movement" Release - ankle rotations under the desk, shoulder shrugs, jaw release.
2. The "Worst-Case Scenario" Roleplay (20 min) - Scenario cards for exam-hall disasters (e.g. "You read Question 5 and you have NO idea what it means", "15 minutes left and 3 essays to write", "The person next to you is sniffing and tapping their pen loudly"). In pairs, a "Panicked Student" and a "Calm Coach" who walks them through a station technique. Key script: "Stop. Breathe. Anchor. Then attack the question you DO know first."
sessions.materials: Metronome or phone timer, pencils, spare paper, laminated scenario/roleplay cards

sessions.title: Passive Brain Break: "The 2-Minute Exam Reset"
sessions.activities: Teens sit upright with eyes closed. Guided visualisation: "Imagine you are sitting in the exam hall. You flip the paper over. Your heart thumps. Now, pause. You place your palms on the desk. You take 3 box breaths. You look at the clock and say to yourself, 'I have time.' You read the first question and underline the keywords. You are calm. You are capable. Open your eyes."

sessions.title: Segment 3: Mindfulness & Study Habits - "Studying Smarter, Not Harder"
sessions.activities:
1. The "Pomodoro vs. Marathon" Race (15 min) - Two teams. Team Marathon writes 1 to 100 without stopping; Team Pomodoro writes 1-20, stands and stretches 30 seconds, then 21-40, and so on. Time them. Debrief: Pomodoro technique, 25 minutes focused revision (phones face down) then a 5-minute active break (walk, stretch, hydrate, no scrolling).
2. The "Revision Roulette" Game (20 min) - Spinner/cards with retrieval techniques: "Blurt it out" (60 seconds on a topic), "Draw it" (diagram/mind-map with no words), "Teach it" (explain like they are 5), "Quiz it" (write 3 exam questions). Spin for a random subject (e.g. Photosynthesis, Quadratic Equations, Macbeth) and revise it on the spot. Script: "Re-reading your notes is like watching a cooking show. Retrieval practice is actually cooking the meal."
3. The "Night-Before & Morning-Of" Blueprint (15 min) - Double-sided Exam Day Blueprint card. Side A, The Night Before: stop-studying time (8 PM max), one relaxing activity, pack your bag now (pens, calculator, water, snack). Side B, The Morning Of: eat protein, 5 minutes of box breathing before leaving, arrive early but avoid panicked friends who are cramming. Keep it in the phone case or pencil case.
sessions.materials: Timer, paper and pens, Revision Roulette spinner/wheel or cards, Exam Day Blueprint cards

sessions.title: Closing & Commitment Ceremony: "The Exam Day Lanyard"
sessions.activities:
The "Lanyard Cue Card": each teen writes ONLY 3 things on a blank laminated card on a string/keyring: My go-to breath (e.g. Box Breath), My anchor (e.g. palms on the desk), My mantra (e.g. "I know more than I think I do."). Wear it as a lanyard or keep it in the pencil case for every exam.
The "Post-Exam" Rule: the 10-Minute Rule, vent to a friend for exactly 10 minutes after an exam, then talk about something else; set a phone timer for it.
Final facilitator script: "Exams don't define your intelligence; they test your ability to retrieve information under artificial pressure. Your body is not your enemy... You have the tools. When you sit down in that hall, you are not alone, you are carrying this entire room with you."

materials: Spinner/wheel or cards for Revision Roulette
Blank laminated cards + keyrings/string for lanyards
Metronome or phone timer (for breathwork station)
notes:
Programme schedule overview: Welcome & Ice-Breaker (10 min); Segment 1 Understanding Exam Stress (50 min); Active Brain Break (5 min); Segment 2 Coping Mechanisms (50 min); Passive Brain Break (5 min); Segment 3 Mindfulness & Study Habits (50 min); Closing (10 min).

Key mantra: "Stop. Breathe. Anchor. Then attack the question you DO know first."

Facilitator note on stress types: you cannot use a "calm-down" technique if you haven't been sleeping well for 3 weeks; chronic and acute stress are treated differently.

Missing details: the document is a run-sheet only; it has no date, venue, facilitators, group size, budget, risk management or evaluation plan.

Source: Mind_Craft_-_stress_Management_Programme.docx

title: The Mixing Bowl - Creative Baking
summary: A customisable baking experience where participants work together in small groups to create Granola Power Bars (granola cups), choosing their own add-ins and toppings. It gives youths a safe space to make self-directed decisions, experiment and make mistakes, and builds agency, communication and basic kitchen life skills. Youths should leave with a greater sense of achievement and better self-confidence.
groupSize: 12 participants (budget based on 12 pax; groups of 3-4)
objectives: Competency in preparing and creating the dish
Greater confidence in self
Building of self-identity and autonomy through self-directed decisions
Engage with peers through a mix of group and individual activities, building communicative and innovative skills
Equip participants with life skills in food preparation and basic kitchen usage

sessions.title: Arrival
sessions.activities: 17:00-17:05 Participants arrive

sessions.title: Introduction and icebreaker: Guess the food
sessions.activities:
17:05-17:25 Introduction of facilitator and icebreaker
Participants are divided into 2 groups.
Each group takes turns sending out 1-2 group members, who are blindfolded.
Small food items are handed out for them to try; they have 2 tries to guess what they ate.
Successful guesses get a point each.
Game ends at first to 3 points or after 5 rounds.
Check allergies and choking hazards before the icebreaker.

sessions.title: Main activity: Granola Power Bars
sessions.activities:
17:25-18:15 Main activity
Divide into groups of 3-4 members; hand out instruction lists; explain general dos and don'ts while baking.
Mix oats, chosen add-ins, salt and dry spices in a bowl.
Warm honey and nut butter slightly (microwave 30 sec) to make it runny, mix into dry ingredients. Add egg white or mashed banana if using.
Press mixture firmly into greased or lined muffin cups to form a cup shape (use back of a spoon to make an indentation).
Bake at 160°C for 12-15 minutes until golden (optional: set in fridge 1 hour for no-bake).
Cool completely, then pop out of tin.
Fill with yogurt, fresh fruit or a dollop of Nutella when serving.
When done, participants pack up and get ready for debrief.
sessions.materials: Base ingredients, customisation bowls, mixing bowl, measuring cups, rubber spatula, mini bowls, oven mitts, baking tray, baking sheet/cups, wax paper, oven, microwave, instruction lists

sessions.title: Debrief and reflection
sessions.activities:
18:15-18:25 Debrief and reflection (allow baked items to cool down)
Survey form and verbal feedback.

sessions.title: Pack up
sessions.activities:
18:25-18:30 Pack up and get ready to leave
18:30 End of session

materials: Honey or maple syrup: 80 ml (or agave for vegan option)
Peanut butter or almond butter: 100 g
Binding help: 1 egg white (baked) or mashed banana (no-bake)
Crunch add-ins: chopped almonds, pumpkin seeds, Rice Krispies, toasted coconut flakes
Sweetness & flavour: mini chocolate chips, dried cranberries or raisins, chopped dried mango or apricot, cinnamon or cocoa powder
Toppings: chocolate chips, yogurt or nut butter drizzle, fresh fruit
budget: ~S$10 for 12 pax (base S$2.60, customisation S$6.20, liners/cooking spray ~S$1.20); ~S$0.83 per pax; total for run S$40
riskNotes:
Centre risk: fall risk in centre (climbing, running and slip risks). Mitigation: proper rules and instructions for all activities; ground rules and consequences for breaking them.

During activity: cuts, bruises or other injuries; burns from mishandling the oven. Mitigation: proper supervision where risk is present; instructions for proper handling; never leave high-risk objects unattended; maintain observation of oven use at all times; no playing with equipment except for intended use.

Food safety: take note of any allergies and choking hazards (during icebreaker).

Psychological safety: sharing is optional; no fixing or judging rule stated; clear group agreements; facilitator models vulnerability appropriately.

Emergency contact: Jeremy, 92243993.
outcomes:
Intended outcomes: youths leave with a greater sense of achievement, better self-confidence and an observable difference in basic life skills.

Success criteria: youths leave satisfied with their product, or feeling motivated to try again, exhibiting a greater desire for autonomy and self-directed decision making.

Feedback: survey form and verbal feedback.
notes:
Target ages ticked on the form: 10–12 (Upper Primary) and 13–16 (Secondary). Format ticked: One-off session.

Venue: Brahm Centre @ Aljunied (no transport; no F&B provided). Date and time listed as TBC in the overview; activity timeline runs 17:00-18:30.

Facilitator: Jeremy (main facilitator).

Attire: comfortable clothes, optional extra clothes to change, jacket, covered shoes.

Recipe yield: makes about 12 cups. Customisation options are set up in bowls for participants to choose: crunch add-ins (pick 1-2), sweetness & flavour (pick 1-2), and post-baking toppings after cups are shaped (chocolate chips pressed on top, drizzle of yogurt or nut butter after cooling, fresh fruit when serving).

Youth need addressed: youths' need for agency and autonomy; making self-directed decisions without external pressure. The centre provides a safe space to experiment, explore and make mistakes, and to engage with peers through group and individual activities.

Why it matters for this age group: a critical period to build a stable self-identity; youths are most curious and open to change, and restricting options can hinder willingness to try new experiences. title: King of the Table (Game On! Night)
summary: Weekly social gathering sessions focused on engagement through board games and social games at Brahm Centre @ Aljunied. Youths get to interact with like-minded peers in a safe space without fear of being judged, build friendships, and take a break from their usual worries and stresses. Along the way they build critical thinking and flexible thinking through strategy and creativity across different games.
objectives: Build self confidence
Foster prosocial behaviour among peers in a safe manner
Build critical thinking and flexible thinking through games
Meet the need for social interaction through play and fun in a safe environment, so participants can build friendships without fear of being judged
Give participants a break from their usual space to escape their worries and stresses

sessions.title: Arrival
sessions.activities: 17:00-17:05 Participants arrive at centre

sessions.title: Icebreaker and introduction: Name Unscrambler
sessions.activities:
17:05-17:20 Icebreaker and introduction
Participants are given a paper each and tasked with writing out the letters in their name (letters should be jumbled up)
Each participant takes turns trying to guess each others' name
1 point awarded for each correct guess
Subsequently, facilitator can change the game: participants spell out as many words as possible using the alphabets in their name

title: Masquerade Mystery – Ex Alumni Christmas Programme
summary: A warm and welcoming Christmas masquerade gathering that bridges the past and the future of the youth community, inviting former interns to reconnect, share stories and reignite old friendships while meeting the newest youth team members. Through casual icebreakers, sharing circles and free-flowing conversation, young adults build social confidence, a sense of belonging and fresh connections.
objectives: Reconnect former interns, share stories and reignite old friendships
Help former interns meet and mingle with the newest youth team members
Build interpersonal communication: initiating conversations, active listening and articulating personal stories
Foster a sense of belonging by bridging past interns with new members, reinforcing that everyone is valued regardless of tenure
Cultivate empathy and awareness through sharing and listening to others' stories

sessions.title: Icebreaker: Behind the Mask
sessions.activities:
Inside your group (5 people): each person takes 2 minutes to share their alias name and their connection to the team (current role, past internship, or how they're involved), and the inspiration behind their mask or costume (why they chose it, what it represents, or if it reflects a hidden talent, personality trait or favourite character)
Group introduction: after everyone has shared, the group selects one representative to introduce all 5 members to the wider room, briefly sharing each person's name and team connection and one memorable highlight from each person's mask or costume story
Rotation (optional): if time permits, groups rotate and mix after 15-20 minutes to meet new people beyond their initial group

sessions.title: Main activity: Human Bingo
sessions.activities:
Prepare the cards: a 5x5 Bingo card per participant with 25 fun, inclusive icebreaker statements (e.g. "Has worn a costume before", "Speaks two or more languages", "Has been to a masquerade"), with a FREE SPACE in the centre
Distribute and explain: hand out one card and a pen to each participant; goal is to mingle and find someone who matches each statement and have them sign that square; no one may sign their own card
Set the timer: announce a time limit (e.g. 20-25 minutes) to circulate, introduce themselves and collect signatures from as many different people as possible
Start mingling: approach others with a friendly introduction and ask if they fit a square; if yes they sign, if no move on
Call BINGO: on completing a row, column or diagonal, participant shouts BINGO and comes to the front; facilitator verifies by having them briefly introduce the people who signed each square
Continue or wrap up: announce additional winners for a full house if time permits
sessions.materials: Human Bingo cards (50, 5 varieties), pens, lucky draw prizes

sessions.title: Debrief
sessions.activities: Gather everyone back; ask a few participants to share one interesting thing they learned about someone new before transitioning to the next activity

sessions.title: Sharing circles, open networking and light dinner
sessions.activities: Sharing circles and free-flowing conversations (talking cards); open networking with spontaneous mingling; light dinner; lucky draw (no detailed run-sheet given)
sessions.materials: Talking cards (10 sets), food, lucky draw prizes

sessions.title: Feedback and close
sessions.activities: Participants complete the feedback form in the last 15 minutes of the session; door gifts

Success criteria: 80% of participants sign up for future programmes; at least 50% willing to come back as volunteers in the near future; at least 80% report feeling more comfortable initiating conversations with new people after the event; participants actively interact with at least 5 different people during Human Bingo; observed increase in spontaneous mingling and peer-to-peer interaction during open networking.

notes:
Venue: Brahm Centre @ Aljunied (youth centre setting), 22 Dec 2026, 6:00-8:00pm. Transport: nil. Food: light dinner.

Facilitators: Jeremy, Raymond – main staff on site; Lyndon, Mei Jing, Xenon – care staff on site.

Attire: smart formal clothes; jacket in case cold. Participants come in mask or costume.

Target age (as ticked): 13-16, 17-19, 20-24 and 25-34; the icebreaker rationale targets 17-25 year olds (former interns and new youth team members).

Core competencies: Think Independently Of Trends; Embrace Discomfort Without Escape; Start And Conduct Conversations. Primary focus: interpersonal communication, built through Behind the Mask and Human Bingo.

Core youth need: sense of belonging and community; continuity and purpose after internships (avoiding engagement drop-off); mentorship and peer learning; emotional safety and validation; transition support between life stages.

Icebreaker: Behind the Mask, 15 minutes; purpose: reduce awkwardness, encourage interaction, build trust and safety, normalise sharing. Suits 17-25s because the masquerade theme allows mature self-expression, builds networking confidence in a low-stakes format, and balances fun with meaningful connection.

How youths are involved: every youth is an active player, moving around the room, initiating conversations and collecting signatures.

Mindfulness element: reflection and insight through mindful listening; infused mid-session, 6-10 minutes; framed as listening to others share their stories and focusing on the details.
